clue.text: Plant with a sting stuck in the chimney

indicators.note: something stuck in a thing sits wedged inside it, so these words go within the outer word

blocks.note: lum is a Scottish and northern English word for a chimney
taken as written
to sting is to smart or burn

explanation.surface: A gardener's warning about a nettle-like plant growing inside a chimney stack.
explanation.walkthrough: Lum is a Scottish word for chimney that crosswords lean on; 'sting' is a verb meaning to smart, not a nettle's barb.
explanation.definitionFit: Laburnum is a small tree with hanging yellow flowers, an example of a garden plant.

clue.text: Reportedly bright criminal devised means of support

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound of the word counts rather than its spelling

blocks.note: bright in the sense of lively and animated
a hood, short for hoodlum, is a gangster

explanation.surface: A clever crook has come up with a way of earning a crust.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, the answer is 'lively hood': the first part needs only the sound of lively, spelt differently in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A livelihood is the job or income by which a person keeps body and soul together.

clue.text: Fabulous thornbird holds key to Shropshire town

indicators.note: fabulous means fabled or invented, so the following word is made up into something new
a thing that holds another keeps it inside, so the rearranged word wraps round the extra letter

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: A mythical bird guarding the key that unlocks a town in Shropshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Shropshire is an English county on the Welsh border; Bridgnorth is a market town on the River Severn there.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridgnorth is a real market town in that western English county, so the place name fits.

clue.text: Slater turned up, having been fired again

indicators.note: in a down entry, a word turned up is read from bottom to top, so its letters run backwards

blocks.note: a slater lays slates on roofs, the work of a tiler

explanation.surface: A roofer showed up after losing a previous job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired' looks like sacking, which suits the slater; here it means set alight, as of a pipe or fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Something relit has been set alight a second time, as a fire or candle burning once more.

clue.text: Free upstanding girl: two students have turned clumsily around

indicators.note: standing up in a down entry means the name is written bottom to top, so backwards
done clumsily, a word is botched and comes out jumbled
around says the jumbled word goes outside the other pieces, enclosing them

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
a girl's name
L, for learner, is a student; two of them

explanation.surface: A respectable young woman freed herself, while a pair of students fumbled about her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' looks like an indicator but is the fodder; L for learner is the crossword student.
explanation.definitionFit: Untrammelled means unrestrained, not hampered by any restriction, which is to be free.

clue.text: Jack on the way to distant climes?

blocks.note: a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman
a road is a way

explanation.surface: A traveller called Jack sets out on the road to far-off lands.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' puts one piece before the other. The question mark admits that 'to distant climes' is a loose way of saying overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: To go abroad is to travel to foreign countries, far-off lands with other weather.

clue.text: Meeting place with offer of food and lodging

blocks.note: board means meals provided, as in bed and board
a room is lodging

explanation.surface: A guest house advert promising a place to gather plus meals and a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board and lodging' is a familiar phrase, which hides that BOARD and ROOM are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A boardroom is the room where a company's directors hold their meetings.

clue.text: Curse that's old hat, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests one arrangement among several, so the letters may be set out differently

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
taken as written

explanation.surface: Swearing is a tired, outdated habit, or so someone suggests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old hat' reads as one idiom meaning stale, but old supplies only its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath can be a swear word or profanity, the same sense as a curse.

clue.text: At Carthage she saw the sights for nothing

blocks.note: to do a city is to go and see its sights, so saw the sights is did
O, the zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: A tourist in ancient Carthage who went sightseeing without paying.
explanation.walkthrough: Dido is the legendary founder and queen of Carthage, abandoned by Aeneas in Virgil's Aeneid.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary queen who founded and ruled the city is the woman meant by this description.

clue.text: Five small English bays suitable for tiny vessels

blocks.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
E is the short form for English
inlets are small bays

explanation.surface: A sailing guide recommending five little English coves for very small boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' suggests boats; here they are blood vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: Veinlets are little veins, minute channels carrying blood in the body, or ribs in a leaf.

clue.text: Stuck with "History Man"

blocks.note: history is the past
Ed is a man's name

explanation.surface: Someone stuck with The History Man, Malcolm Bradbury's campus novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make a single title of two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasted means fixed with glue or paste, so attached in place like something stuck.

clue.text: Noisy cry said to be caused by a personality trait

indicators.note: the trait is said to produce these words, so they are the raw material reshaped into its name

blocks.note: every letter of these three words is used

explanation.surface: A psychologist explains that someone's loud shout comes from a quirk of character.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiosyncrasy is a peculiar habit or quirk belonging to one individual, a trait of their personality.

clue.text: Dexter changing sides develops a delicate touch

definitions.note: a noun phrase for an adjective: light-handed means having a delicate touch

indicators.note: changing sides swaps right for left, so one side's letter replaces the other's

blocks.note: dexter is Latin and heraldic for right, and a dexter person favours the right hand

explanation.surface: A right-handed person who switches hands discovers a gentle touch.
explanation.walkthrough: R for right becomes L for left. Dexter looks like a name; it is Latin for right.
explanation.definitionFit: Light-handed describes deft, gentle handling, a soft deft touch with the hands.

clue.text: Old curiosities cross to the New World

blocks.note: the Victoria Cross is Britain's highest award for gallantry
NA stands for North America

explanation.surface: Antique oddities ship across the Atlantic to America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a verb of travel; it stands for the Victoria Cross, the British military medal.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoriana are collectable objects from the reign of Queen Victoria, antiques and curios from that era.

clue.text: Two chits - right? - required for the plant

indicators.note: the letters are required, that is called up and put into service, in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
RT is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A query about whether two notes are needed to get hold of a certain plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Stitchwort is a white-flowered hedgerow plant of the pink family, once used for a stitch in the side.

clue.text: Catches the blows

blocks.note: first meaning: fastenings, or catches as a fish is caught
second meaning: curving punches in boxing

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a goalkeeper or boxer parrying punches; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooks fasten or snag things, and in boxing a hook is a short swinging punch.

clue.text: Garden tool Tiger hauled into the Bishop's office, pursued by Bear? Almost!

indicators.note: dragged into somewhere means being placed inside it
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is left off
being pursued means being followed, so the next piece comes after

blocks.note: a see is a bishop's diocese or seat of office
a tiger is a big cat
Ursa is Latin for bear, as in the constellation Ursa Major

explanation.surface: A tiger dragged into the bishop's palace with a bear on its tail, nearly.
explanation.definitionFit: Secateurs are pruning shears, a hand cutting implement for trimming plants and branches.

clue.text: My love, for the record, is starting training as a muscleman

indicators.note: starting points to the beginning of the next word, so only its opening letter is used

blocks.note: taken as written
love is a zero score in tennis, and zero looks like O
a log is a written record
taken as written
the opening letter of training

explanation.surface: Someone tells their sweetheart they have begun working out to become a bodybuilder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muscleman' suggests a bodybuilder; here it is a scientist who studies muscles.
explanation.definitionFit: A myologist is an expert in the anatomy of muscles, so jokingly a man of muscle.

clue.text: Measure topless girl by sight

indicators.note: without its top, a word in an across clue loses its first letter

blocks.note: an optic is the device on an upturned bottle in a British pub that dispenses a measure of spirits
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A man sizes up a topless young woman with his eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Optically means visually, with regard to the eye or vision, which is judging by sight.

clue.text: Alien following cat around with hymnal music

indicators.note: turned around, a word faces the other way and is read backwards
following means coming after, so the alien is placed second, behind the turned cat

blocks.note: a tom is a male cat
ET, the extra-terrestrial, is an alien

explanation.surface: A space creature chasing a cat round and round while carrying a hymn book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts ET after the turned-around cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A motet is a short sacred choral composition, church music sung like a hymn.

clue.text: Fetch Ron the rum after that

indicators.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange, so the words before it are made strange

blocks.note: every letter of these three words is used

explanation.surface: A request to bring Ron his rum, and then something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The rum' reads as the drink; rum is the indicator and 'the' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Thenceforth is an old-fashioned adverb meaning from that time on, onward from then.

clue.text: Archaic song, loud yet madly out of tune

indicators.note: something done madly is wild and disordered, so the letters are scrambled
a letter taken out of a word is drawn from it, here its first

blocks.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
taken as written
the opening letter of tune

explanation.surface: An old ballad sung loudly and wildly off key.
explanation.definitionFit: A fytte is an archaic term for a section or canto of a poem or ballad.

clue.text: Buy such talk?

blocks.note: first meaning: go buying goods
second meaning: talk about work, in the phrase talking it

explanation.walkthrough: The second half defines by example: the answer is the kind of talk in the phrase for discussing one's work out of hours, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for making purchases and also names conversation about one's job.

clue.text: Bellies up! Bit of rudeness

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written from the bottom, so backwards

blocks.note: tums is informal for stomachs

explanation.surface: Bellies up, like a crude cheer in a pub, is itself a bit rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is indecent or obscene talk or material, a piece of crude vulgarity.

clue.text: Pander to wit

blocks.note: first meaning: indulge someone, go along with their whims
second meaning: comic quality, funniness

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as advice to flatter a clever person; the verb and the noun are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means indulge someone's wishes, and as a noun it means comedy or funniness.

clue.text: Small insect, one in a pudding in Chile

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the word that follows

blocks.note: sago is a starchy milk pudding
an ant is a small insect
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A diner finds a little bug lurking in a dessert served in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a place found in Chile: its capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Santiago is the capital of Chile, so it is a city located in that South American country.

clue.text: Remains of drug in fertilizer

blocks.note: pot is slang for cannabis
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: Traces of a narcotic turn up in some garden plant food.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are written in the reverse of the clue order: drug first, then remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Potash is a potassium compound widely spread on fields as plant food.

clue.text: Mechanical writing found to be lacking in diversity

blocks.note: type is print produced by a machine, as from a typewriter
to found metal is to cast it in a mould

explanation.surface: Machine-made text is judged monotonous and samey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past of find; it is the verb for melting and moulding metal, as in a foundry.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor typecast always plays the same sort of role, so their career lacks variety.
